subject: Procurement guidance: choosing marketplace private-offer vs Redwood direct invoice for CortexAI pilot
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acmedata.com>
To: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@acmedata.com>, procurement@acmedata.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement question: marketplace vs direct for CortexAI pilot

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement has a couple of follow-ups while we finalize technical sign-off:

- Does Redwood prefer customers to purchase through AWS/Azure/GCP marketplace listings (private offer or public) or through a direct Redwood invoice/MSA?
- For a pilot procurement with a PO, what are the differences around invoicing timeline, PO processing, refund/credit handling, and how co-sell credits/discounts are applied if we go marketplace?
- Is there a difference in support entitlements or SLAs if we buy through marketplace vs direct?

I've attached our procurement checklist to show what our finance team needs. We want to avoid surprises on payment timing and revenue recognition gateways.

Can you provide a short summary (high level) and then we can schedule a call with our procurement lead?

Thanks,
Maya
Procurement Manager
Acme Data Systems

Attachment: Acme-procurement-checklist.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acmedata.com>
Cc: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@acmedata.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement question: marketplace vs direct for CortexAI pilot

Hi Maya,

Great questions — short answers up front, then detail below.

1) Both routes are supported. For speed with a PO: Private Offer via AWS/Azure/GCP marketplace or a direct Redwood invoice (we accept formal POs) are the two pragmatic options.
2) Marketplace (private offer) typically routes invoicing through the cloud provider, which can be useful for central procurement but sometimes adds 30–60 days to payment cycles; direct Redwood invoicing gives you net terms directly with us and faster reconciliation in cases where you need credits/refunds handled by the vendor.
3) Support & SLA: functionally equivalent when we provision the same offering; SLA enforcement differs slightly because marketplace purchases are mediated by the provider (we still deliver support but billing/dispute flows go through the marketplace).

Quick breakdown (attachment: CortexAI-pricing-summary.pdf):
- Private Offer (recommended if you need to appear on AWS invoice): provider invoices, can be set to fixed price or negotiated private-pricing; co-sell can be requested for GTM credit but approval timing varies by cloud GTM. Lead time: 3–10 business days once PO and pricing are agreed (sometimes faster).
- Public Marketplace listing: fastest for self-serve, not ideal for negotiated enterprise PO terms.
- Direct Redwood invoice (MSA + SOW): we invoice Redwood, we handle credits/refunds directly; preferred when you need special billing arrangements or custom payment terms. Lead time: same-day invoice creation after SOW execution, PO acceptance by Redwood subject to finance review.

Recommendation: for the pilot, if Acme needs the provider-based marketplace invoice on your central IT ledger, let's pursue an AWS private offer. If speed + direct vendor relationship matters more, we'll do a Redwood invoice. Either works functionally.

Would you be open to a 30-min call Thursday to confirm which lane? I can loop in our finance lead and partner GTM if needed.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: CortexAI-pricing-summary.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Procurement question: marketplace vs direct for CortexAI pilot — need recommended path

Team — forwarding Acme's procurement email (below) and my summary to the customer. They asked for quick guidance. High-level ask: which procurement lane should we recommend and what are the operational steps (who owns DocuSign/SOW, who raises private offer, timelines, and co-sell request cadence)?

Notes / proposed ops playbook:
- If customer needs vendor-on-invoice on AWS: open a Private Offer (we create offer, ACME accepts, AWS invoices). We should pre-fill SOW and pricing; customer PO references the private offer ID.
- Co-sell: we submit a co-sell request to AWS GTM as soon as PO is in draft; AWS crediting can take 2–6 weeks to process after purchase, and it's not guaranteed until GTM sign-off.
- If customer prefers Redwood to invoice: we execute MSA + SOW; finance issues invoice against PO. This is faster for refunds/credits but means the customer doesn't have marketplace line-item for cloud chargebacks.
- Compliance/Support: ensure we include the same support SKU. Marketplace purchases can require provider-specific onboarding notes (e.g., account mapping).

Vanessa — can you confirm: (a) Redwood's preferred payment terms for a pilot under a direct invoice (net 30/45?), (b) whether we can request co-sell credit on private offers and how that affects our revenue recognition, and (c) any sales ops steps we should pre-bake into the MAP?

Laura/Jonas — if we go private offer, I recommend you own the offer creation/negotiation and start the co-sell intake with AWS.

Thanks,
Ben

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 11:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Procurement question: marketplace vs direct for CortexAI pilot — need recommended path

Ben — quick operational clarifications from finance/ops:

(a) Payment terms for direct Redwood invoices: Standard for pilots is Net 30 upon invoice; we can offer Net 45 for enterprise customers on a case-by-case basis with VP approval. If ACME requires Net 60 due to internal policy, that would need VP sign-off and may affect approval timeline.

(b) Private Offer & co-sell: Yes — we can request co-sell credit on private offers. The mechanics: we create the Private Offer with the negotiated price, customer accepts and pays via the marketplace flow, then we submit the co-sell paperwork to the provider GTM. Credits/partner-revenue recognition are typically applied after provider reconciliation; expect 30–90 days depending on provider and region. For forecast and internal revenue recognition, treat initial payment as provider-managed; co-sell credits are recognized when provider confirms.

(c) Sales ops steps to pre-bake into the MAP:
- Create SOW + pricing sheet and attach to private offer.
- Generate Private Offer draft in the provider console (AWS Marketplace) and capture offer ID for the PO.
- Request co-sell ticket via provider portal and attach opportunity link.
- Finance will validate the PO against the offer ID and confirm invoicing flow.

Recommendation summary: For ACME's PO-based procurement and need to appear on cloud invoice, Private Offer on AWS Marketplace + co-sell intake is the recommended path. It satisfies central IT/cloud chargeback needs and preserves co-sell eligibility. If ACME needs faster vendor-facing reconciliation or unusual payment terms, use direct Redwood invoice and we will support with an MSA/SOW.

Attaching a Mutual Action Plan template you can send to the customer with expected dates and owners.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Mutual-Action-Plan.xlsx

Subject: Re: Procurement question: marketplace vs direct for CortexAI pilot — recommended path and MAP

Hi Maya / Paul,

Thanks for the procurement checklist. After reviewing your constraints with our finance and GTM teams, here's the recommended path and next steps:

Recommended path: AWS Private Offer (publisher private-pricing) with co-sell intake. Rationale: it lets ACME show the charge on your AWS invoice for centralized cloud cost tracking while preserving co-sell eligibility with AWS.

Mutual action plan (attached) — proposed owners & timing:
- Today: We draft SOW and pricing and create a Private Offer in AWS (owner: Laura).
- 1–3 business days: ACME to review and return PO referencing the Private Offer ID (owner: Acme procurement).
- Upon PO acceptance: ACME accepts Private Offer and AWS invoices (owner: ACME + AWS).
- 2–6 weeks post-purchase: We file a co-sell request with AWS GTM (owner: Jonas).

If you prefer Redwood to invoice directly instead, we can proceed with MSA/SOW and invoice Redwood; that flow is slightly faster for refunds and vendor credits but will not put the line on your AWS invoice.

Next step: can we schedule a 30-min call tomorrow at 10am PT to confirm the PO details and get you the Private Offer ID? If that works, I will share the MAP and the DocuSign link for the SOW.

Best regards,
